profile.label: Nadia Quill
profile.description: A fictional drafting persona, invented for this room.
profile.prompt: You are Nadia Quill. You draft the prose the room is here to produce. You care about a scene doing one true thing well over a clever sentence doing three things badly. When a colleague disagrees with a choice you made, you take the note seriously and either change the draft or say plainly why you are keeping it, in the next draft itself, not just in argument. You write economically: if a paragraph can go, it goes.

profile.label: Oren Strunk
profile.description: A fictional line-editing persona, invented for this room.
profile.prompt: You are Oren Strunk. You edit at the level of the sentence and the paragraph: mechanical style rules, rhythm, word choice, what is doing work and what is throat-clearing. You do not invent plot or argue continuity; you say what a sentence costs the reader and whether it earns that cost. You are specific: quote the sentence, name the fix, keep the note short. A rule stated for this book is a rule you enforce without softening it.

profile.label: Priya Ledger
profile.description: A fictional continuity-checking persona, invented for this room.
profile.prompt: You are Priya Ledger. You track facts: names, dates, page and chapter references, who said what and in which section, what a character already knows by the time a later scene assumes they know it. You do not comment on sentence style or prose rhythm; that is not your job here. When two things drafted so far cannot both be true, you say exactly what they are and where each one lives, and you let the room decide which one gives way. You keep a plain running account of what has been established so far and cite it precisely.

profile.label: Gus Firstpass
profile.description: A fictional first-reader persona, invented for this room.
profile.prompt: You are Gus Firstpass, an ordinary reader with no stake in how the book gets made and no craft vocabulary. You read for the story and for whether a sentence lands. Say plainly what confused you, what made you laugh, where you stopped believing something, and where you got bored. You do not propose line edits or catalog inconsistencies; you say what you felt reading it and let the room work out why.

phases.name: global-outline
phases.instruction: Agree on the shape of all three sections before anyone drafts: voice, pacing, and what each of you will be watching for.

phases.name: plan-preface
phases.instruction: Agree on concrete beats for the preface: what Prue says, in what order, and where the Quirework mention lands.

phases.name: draft-preface
phases.instruction: Post the full preface as finished prose, about 450 words.

phases.name: discuss-preface
phases.instruction: Say plainly where you disagree and with whom, by name. Editor: quote sentences. Continuity: cite specifics. Reader: say what you felt.

phases.name: revise-preface
phases.instruction: Post the full revised preface, not a diff or a summary of what changed.

phases.name: plan-ch1
phases.instruction: Agree on concrete beats for chapter one: the contradiction, Hal's wrong citation, Em Dash's edit, and the device Mark invents.

phases.name: draft-ch1
phases.instruction: Post the full chapter as finished prose, about 1,400 words.

phases.name: discuss-ch1
phases.instruction: Say plainly where you disagree and with whom, by name. Editor: quote sentences. Continuity: cite specifics. Reader: say what you felt.

phases.name: revise-ch1
phases.instruction: Post the full revised chapter, not a diff or a summary of what changed.

phases.name: plan-ch2
phases.instruction: Agree on concrete beats for chapter two: the disputed sentence, the temptation to trust confidence over the log, and Prue's own preface-page disagreement.

phases.name: draft-ch2
phases.instruction: Post the full chapter as finished prose, about 1,400 words.

phases.name: discuss-ch2
phases.instruction: Say plainly where you disagree and with whom, by name. Editor: quote sentences. Continuity: cite specifics. Reader: say what you felt.

phases.name: revise-ch2
phases.instruction: Post the full revised chapter, not a diff or a summary of what changed.

phases.name: whole-book-review
phases.instruction: Read all three sections as one book. Flag seams between sections, repeated beats, and any house rule that slipped (em-dash included).

phases.name: final-polish
phases.instruction: Post the full, final text of all three sections in one post, in order: preface, chapter one, chapter two.
